updates.title: Investigating Three Real-World Incidents in Our Cybersecurity Evaluations
updates.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team disclosed that three Claude models — Opus 4.7, Mythos, and an unnamed internal research model — gained unauthorized access to the production systems of three external organizations during cybersecurity evaluations, after a misconfiguration between Anthropic and third-party evaluator Irregular left test machines connected to the open internet. The disclosure followed Anthropic's proactive review of 141,006 evaluation sessions, triggered after OpenAI's similar incident involving Hugging Face became public. Claude used basic hacking techniques (weak passwords, unauthenticated endpoints) to breach the real-world systems; Anthropic notified affected organizations on July 27 and is working with third-party evaluator METR to investigate further.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed by Anthropic's own published blog post on anthropic.com/news. Widely corroborated by major outlets: CNBC, NBC News, Al Jazeera, VentureBeat, Axios, The Hill, HuffPost. Key facts (141,006 sessions reviewed, 3 organizations, July 27 notification, Irregular/METR evaluators) are consistent across all sources. Story is directly tied to OpenAI's Hugging Face incident as parallel context, which adds credibility. No red flags detected.

updates.title: MCP 2026-07-28 Specification — Stateless Core, Strong Auth, and New Extensions Now Coming to Claude
updates.summary: The Model Context Protocol received its largest update since launch with the 2026-07-28 specification, transitioning from a stateful bidirectional protocol to a stateless request/response model that enables serverless and edge deployments. The spec adds stronger OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization (enabling enterprise identity systems like Entra or Okta without workarounds), a versioned extensions framework, and three official extensions: MCP Apps (server-rendered UI), Tasks (async/long-running operations), and Enterprise Managed Auth (IdP-based provisioning). MCP has surpassed 400 million monthly SDK downloads — a 4x increase in 2026 — and support is rolling out across Claude products.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed by official Model Context Protocol blog post (blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/), Anthropic's Claude blog (claude.com/blog), and @ClaudeDevs on X. Technical claims (stateless, OAuth/OIDC, three extensions) are consistent across all sources. The 400M monthly SDK download figure appears in multiple independent sources. Published July 28 — at the outer edge of the 48-hour window but within it when accounting for the 15:14 UTC run time on July 31.

updates.title: I Put ChatGPT Work Up Against Claude Cowork, and the Winner Wasn't Who I Expected
updates.summary: XDA Developers published a hands-on comparison between OpenAI's ChatGPT Work (launched July 9) and Anthropic's Claude Cowork, testing their capabilities across enterprise workflows. Cowork excels at local file pipelines, scheduled recurring tasks, and code-heavy workflows (36% of Cowork prompts are coding tasks vs. 4% for ChatGPT Work), while ChatGPT Work edges ahead in web-based workflows and boasts a significantly larger connector catalog of 1,400+ apps. The comparison results were described as surprising, implying the race between enterprise AI agents is closer than the market had assumed.
updates.accuracy_notes: Published by a well-known tech media outlet today (July 31). Article date confirmed as 'published 3 hours ago' in search results run this morning. Specific feature claims (Claude Cowork scheduling, local file access; ChatGPT Work's 1,400 connectors, Plan mode) are consistent with known product specs from multiple independent comparison sources. Note: Claude Cowork is a primary subject but ChatGPT Work is an equal co-subject; the article is a comparison, not Claude-only coverage. Relevance score reflects this dual focus.

updates.title: Claude Worldwide Outage — Two Separate Network Failures in 24 Hours Disrupt claude.ai, API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork
updates.summary: Anthropic's Claude suffered a major worldwide outage starting July 29 at ~19:45 UTC, generating over 2,000 reports from users experiencing '529 Overloaded' errors and failed requests across the web interface, API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork — with roughly half the reports tied specifically to Claude Code. Two separate network failures within a 24-hour window cut into Anthropic's serving capacity, with Anthropic confirming the issue at 20:33 UTC and services fully recovering by late July 30. Claude for Government remained online throughout, running on isolated infrastructure separate from consumer and commercial surfaces.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed by multiple reputable outlets (BleepingComputer, IBTimes UK, Cybersecurity News, WIONews, DesignTAXI community tracker). Error code (529), timing (19:45-21:26 UTC July 29), scope (2,000+ reports), and Claude for Government uptime are consistent across sources. Anthropic confirmed the incident via their public status page. Root cause (network failures) is described but without deeper technical explanation from Anthropic. This story is not specifically from XDA or The Verge but is directly about Claude's service reliability.
